data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): opposite (clearly visible as paired leaves emerging from the same nodes along the stem in multiple images)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): distal (leaves are spaced along the stem with clear internodes visible)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3.	Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single blade without leaflets)
    4.	Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5.	Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6.	Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7.	Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): toothed (fine serrations are visible along the leaf margins)
    8.	Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (leaf is broadest in the middle and tapers towards both ends)
    9.	Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (leaf tip tapers to a distinct point)
    10.	Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (leaf base tapers to a wedge shape)
    11.	Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (single midrib with lateral veins branching off)
    12.	Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): clearly visible, relatively close spacing, numerous
    13.	Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): glabrous, somewhat shiny (leaf surface appears smooth and reflects light slightly)
    14.	Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no hairs visible on the leaf surface)
    15.	Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are relatively short compared to the leaf blade)
    16.	Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles appear round in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17.	Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (stem appears green and flexible, typical of a young seedling)
    18.	Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (stem appears smooth without visible hairs)
    19.	Stem color: green (stem is predominantly green)
    20.	Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (stem surface appears smooth)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21.	Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules clearly visible at the leaf bases)
    22.	Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no latex is visible)
    23.	Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no pulvinus is visible at the leaf base)
    24.	Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils are visible)
F. Notes: Some leaves show minor damage in the form of small holes. Some leaves exhibit light-colored mottling or spotting on the surface.
